records.name: Strategy & Board Games Club at Wharton
records.summary: A campus club at the Wharton School that runs weekly game nights, small group board game sessions and game tournaments. It also runs a game expo to help newcomers find games they enjoy.
records.what_you_do: Show up for a small group session, learn a new game, or join a tournament or Game Fam night.

schedule.text: Weekly game nights, plus small group board game sessions on listed evenings: October 20 (7 to 9 pm), October 22 (6:30 to 9:30 pm) and October 27 (6:45 to 9:15 pm)

first_step.how: Use the club's sign-up form, linked from the club's site
first_step.basis: The page says gamers at all levels are welcome and mentions a newcomer game expo, but it does not say whether non-Penn people can join, so the way in is unclear

records.notes: The October event dates show no year on the page, so the newest dated evidence cannot be placed in time. The page does not say who may join, so open_to is set to students only because the club's focus is on students. Confirm eligibility before relying on it. Found by web search, not from a Meetup page.

records.name: Drinks and Dragons
records.summary: A roleplaying group that meets in Philadelphia bars so anyone can sit down at a table. Players use Dungeons and Dragons and other tabletop roleplaying games, and experienced players help newcomers learn the rules.
records.what_you_do: Join a table for about three hours, roll dice, and play a story with the group. You buy your own food and drinks.

schedule.text: Every third Wednesday at one bar and every first Thursday at another bar, about three hours each

cost.text: No admission charge. You buy your own food and drinks.

first_step.how: Check the group's Facebook page for the next session
first_step.basis: The article says anyone can come, prior rules knowledge is not needed, and experienced players help newcomers; the Facebook page is the way in

records.notes: The only source is a magazine article first published October 2017 and last updated February 2025, so the schedule and venues may be out of date. No official website exists; the group names a Facebook page. Venue addresses are not published in the article. Age rules for the bars are not stated. Found by web search, not from a Meetup page.

records.name: The Phoenix Philadelphia
records.summary: A nonprofit community for people in recovery, the people who love them, and anyone who wants friends without alcohol or drugs. Its Philadelphia programs include workouts, art, social meetups and other free events.
records.what_you_do: Go to free sober activities led by volunteers, such as fitness sessions, art, or social meetups. A sober community center is planned for North Philadelphia.

schedule.text: Events are posted on the website; the page checked lists no weekly schedule or dates

locations.label: Philadelphia, PA (addresses not published on the page checked)

cost.text: Programs are free, according to the website

first_step.how: Download The Phoenix app or use the Contact Us page on the website
first_step.basis: Open to people in recovery, families, and anyone seeking connection, with a clear way to contact or join; no beginner program is described

records.notes: The site is working but shows no dated events, so status is probably_active by the rule for working sites with no dates. The page does not state a sobriety-time requirement for events, so none is recorded. A North Philadelphia center was described as starting in spring 2026; not confirmed as open. Found by web search, not from a Meetup page.

records.name: We Walk PHL
records.summary: A free walking group run through Philadelphia Parks and Recreation that meets in public parks across the city. Trained local leaders guide about an hour of walking, one to three times a week depending on the park.
records.what_you_do: Walk with neighbors for about an hour in a park near you, and get to know people who walk the same route.

schedule.text: One to three walks a week depending on the park, during the fall season from September 1 to October 31. Days and times are posted on the program's Facebook page.

locations.label: Public parks across Philadelphia (varies by site)

first_step.how: Register through the We Walk PHL portal on GivePulse, or check the program's Facebook page for the nearest walk
first_step.basis: Free and described as open to neighbors, with a registration portal; eligibility rules are not stated

records.notes: The city announcement is dated September 10, 2025 and names no year for the fall season, so the newest evidence is a little over a year old. Walk times and park names are only on the Facebook page, which was not read. The GivePulse portal is a platform, used only as a sign-up link, not as a source.

records.name: Philadelphia Front Runners
records.summary: An LGBTQIA+ running and walking club for athletes and allies at every pace. Members meet on Saturday mornings at Lloyd Hall on Boathouse Row for a run or walk at their own speed.
records.what_you_do: Run or walk at your own pace with the group on Saturday mornings, then talk with other members.

first_step.how: Go to Lloyd Hall on a Saturday morning; the event listing calls it open to all paces
first_step.basis: A third party event listing says it is open to LGBTQIA+ athletes and allies at all paces, free to attend, with a clear meeting place and time

records.notes: No official website was found in search, so the club's Facebook and Strava pages are the contacts. The main source is a Philadelphia LGBTQ event calendar, a third party listing, not the club itself; its newest listing is dated October 10, 2026. Older magazine guides gave different weekday meetings, which were not used. Found by web search, not from a Meetup page.

notes: Only 5 records were checked and written, below the 20 to 40 target. The binding limit was the WebSearch budget: all 8 searches were used. The Meetup board games topic page loaded but listed no groups in the readable text, and the LGBTQ topic page gave group names only, so most Meetup leads are in leads_only without own websites. Two of the five records (Drinks and Dragons, Philadelphia Front Runners) rely on third party event and article pages, not the groups' own sites, and the groups have no official website found. Many trivia listings in search were bars or venues, which are businesses, so they were not recorded. Join Philly was not a source for this slice. Status is probably_active or unknown on several records because the dated evidence is older than 12 months or missing. Platform pages used: 2 of 12.
